title: Scivias study - New biomarkers for diseases in childhood
summary: The overall goal of this study is to identify new biomarkers for children with rare and chronic diseases. Based on these findings, we wish to design new preventive strategies. Eye examinations, in particular imaging of the fundus, hold great promise to define the general state of health in adults. Here, we wish to analyze fundoscopy in children to define markers of diseases that do not primarily affect the eye. This may allow us to define chronic diseases earlier. Furthermore, we will acquire detailed phenotypic data and a comprehensive analysis of proteins and metabolic products as well as genetic information in the blood and urine. Examination of the fundus is a routine method in ophthalmology, no application of drugs is needed for widening the pupils. Therefore, there is no impairment of vision. To examine the gene products (RNA - transcriptome and proteins - proteome) and metabolic products (so-called metabolome) as well as the individually different genome data (OMICS data) in blood, a blood sample will be taken. With the help of new mathematic algorithms, the information (eye images, genome, transcriptome, metabolome and proteome) will be analyzed in order to gain new insights into genes and signal pathways and discover biomarkers associated with chronic diseases in children.
conditions: Diseases in childhood with an emphasis on disorders of the immune system and metabolism

interventions.name: In the study images of the retina are taken using non-invasive methods of fundus photography, optical coherence tomography (OCT) and OCT angiography (thanks to technical advances mydriasis is not necessary).
